options.name: label
options.description: The text of the button in the task. Defaults to the title of the rule.

options.name: cron
options.description: A cron expression with five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), evaluated in the time zone of the server (service.timezone). Example: 0 9 * * 1 is every Monday at 09:00.

options.name: scope
options.description: tasks: one run per task of the project that matches the conditions (at most automation.ticker.maxtasks per tick). project: one run per tick without a task; use it with a create task action first.

options.name: offset
options.description: How long before the due date the rule fires, e.g. 24h or 2d.

options.name: secret
options.description: The name of a project secret. When set, every call has to carry the header X-Vikunja-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body, keyed with the secret>.

params.name: source
params.description: The body of a function, for example: `const parent = vikunja.tasks.get(task.id); return parent.title;`. Statements run in strict mode. Not a template: {{placeholders}} are not replaced.

actions.description: Runs JavaScript with the permissions of the rule owner. The source is the body of a function: use return to give a result, which is stored (as JSON) in the output of the step. A thrown error fails the step. See the script reference for the globals and the limits.

params.name: mode
params.description: any: the first decision resolves the request. all: every approver has to approve, one rejection rejects.

actions.description: Asks people to approve the task: an ad-hoc approval request that changes no status. The request is made by the owner of the rule, who cannot be one of the approvers. The approvers need to be able to read the task.

Creates a task in the project of the rule, as the owner of the rule. When the run has no task (incoming webhook, schedule per project) the new task becomes the task of the actions after it. Text parameters are templates, so they can use {{event.payload.<path>}} of a webhook.

Pauses the run. The actions after this one run later; the pause is stored in the database, so it survives a restart. The conditions are not evaluated again. Minimum 1 minute, maximum automation.waitmax (30 days by default).

params.name: recipients
params.description: User ids and/or the keywords event_doer, task_creator and assignees.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Every member of this team gets the notification, too.

actions.description: Sends an in-app notification (and an e-mail when the person has e-mail notifications on) to people who can read the project. Anybody without access to the project is skipped.

params.name: url
params.description: The address, http or https. Placeholders are replaced; {{secrets.NAME}} is not allowed here.

params.name: method
params.description: The HTTP method. Defaults to POST.

params.name: headers
params.description: Request headers: header name to value. Values are templates and may contain {{secrets.NAME}}. Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection and Upgrade cannot be set.

params.name: body
params.description: The request body. Placeholders and {{secrets.NAME}} are replaced. The Content-Type is application/json when the body is valid JSON and no Content-Type header is given, otherwise text/plain.

params.name: secret
params.description: The name of a project secret. When set, the request carries the header X-Vikunja-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body, keyed with the secret>.

actions.description: Sends an HTTP request to an external service, for example a chat webhook. Private, loopback and link-local addresses are blocked. A 5xx answer or a network error is retried like any temporary failure; a 4xx answer fails the run. The status and the first 2 KiB of the answer are stored in the step output.

script.action_convention: The source is the body of a function: write statements and use return to give a result. The result is stored as JSON in the output of the step. A thrown error fails the step; the message and the line and column are recorded. The code runs in strict mode.
script.condition_convention: The source is the body of a function that must return a value with return; it is converted to true or false. A script that returns nothing (undefined) or ends with a bare expression instead of return fails with a clear error. Condition scripts have a read-only API and a shorter timeout.

limits.name: Scripts enabled
limits.description: When off, rules with scripts cannot be saved and existing ones fail without running.

limits.name: Script timeout
limits.description: The script is stopped and the step fails.

limits.name: Condition script timeout
limits.description: The condition script is stopped and the run fails.

limits.name: HTTP body size (bytes)
limits.description: Request bodies above it are refused, response bodies are cut off.

limits.name: Log output per step (bytes)
limits.description: The rest of the log is dropped.

limits.name: HTTP request timeout
limits.description: Applies to every outgoing request, whatever a script asks for.

api.name: event
api.signature: event: {name, task_id, project_id, doer: {id, username, name}, old, new, changed, field_id}
api.description: The trigger event. Read-only (frozen). old and new hold the values the event knows (see the condition fields event.old.* and event.new.*).

api.name: task
api.signature: task: {id, title, description, done, priority, percent_done, due_date, start_date, end_date, done_at, created, updated, hex_color, identifier, project_id, created_by, assignees, labels, status, custom_fields, relations} | null
api.description: The task the rule runs for, as it is when the script starts. Dates are RFC 3339 strings or null; assignees and labels are lists of ids; status is {id, title, category} or null; custom_fields maps the id of a custom field to its value; relations maps a relation kind (subtask, parenttask, related, blocking, ...) to the list of task ids. Frozen. null for task.deleted.

api.name: project
api.description: The project of the rule. Frozen.

api.name: vikunja.tasks.get
api.description: Reads a task the rule owner may read. Same shape as the global task.

api.name: vikunja.tasks.find
api.description: Finds tasks with the filter syntax of the task list, for example "done = false && cf_12 > 5". Only tasks the rule owner may read are returned, at most the configured maximum. options.project_id limits the search to one project. The result is not paginated.

api.name: vikunja.tasks.update
api.description: Changes a task as the rule owner. patch may contain title, description, priority (0-5), percent_done (0-1), hex_color, done, and due_date, start_date, end_date as an RFC 3339 string, a plain date, a relative value (+3d, -12h, now+1w) or "none" to clear. Plain text is used as it is; {{placeholders}} are not replaced.

api.name: vikunja.tasks.create
api.description: Creates a task in a project the rule owner may write to. data: title (required), description, priority, percent_done, hex_color, due_date, start_date, end_date (as in update), assignees (list of user ids) and parent_id (makes the new task a subtask of that task).

api.name: vikunja.tasks.comment
api.description: Adds a comment (plain text) to a task.

api.name: vikunja.fields.get
api.description: Reads the value of a custom field of a task: a number, string, boolean, a list for multi-select and user fields, or null.

api.name: vikunja.fields.set
api.description: Sets a custom field of a task. Select fields take option ids, date fields take date strings, null clears the value.

api.name: vikunja.status.set
api.description: Moves a task to a workflow status through the normal transition checks of the project.

api.name: vikunja.assignees.add
api.description: Assigns a user to a task. Does nothing when the user is assigned already.

api.name: vikunja.assignees.remove
api.description: Removes an assignee from a task.

api.name: vikunja.labels.add
api.description: Adds a label to a task.

api.name: vikunja.labels.remove
api.description: Removes a label from a task.

api.name: http.fetch
api.signature: http.fetch(url, {method?, headers?, body?, timeout?}) -> {status, ok, headers, body, truncated, json()}
api.description: Sends an HTTP request. Only http and https; private, loopback and link-local addresses are blocked; at most three redirects. method defaults to GET, headers is an object of strings, body a string, timeout in milliseconds (capped). body of the answer is cut off at the configured size. A network error or a blocked address throws; an HTTP error status does not. json() parses the body.

api.name: secrets.get
api.description: Returns the value of a project secret. Throws when the secret does not exist or cannot be decrypted. The value is masked in all stored output and errors. In a test run it returns a placeholder.

api.name: log
api.description: Writes to the output of the step. Objects are written as JSON. console.log is an alias. The total size is limited.
